grammar.title: 半天 and 半年 for stretches of time
grammar.explanation: 半 ("half") combines with time words to describe a duration: 半天 ("half a day", often used loosely to mean "a long while"), 半年 ("half a year"). Place the resulting phrase where any duration or time word would go.

grammar.title: verb + 一下儿 for a quick action
grammar.explanation: Adding 一下儿 (yíxiàr) right after a verb makes the action sound brief, casual, or low-pressure — similar to "just a second" in English: 看一下儿 ("take a quick look"), 等一下儿 ("wait a moment"). It softens requests, making them sound more polite.

sentences.en: He studied for half a year.
We meet once every half year.
